scene_refinement.what: rotation_matrix corrected so cam1 lines up VERTICALLY with cam0 on real footage. Only the two rotations that move cam1 up/down in the overlap were changed - pitch about the horizontal axis at the seam, roll about the seam view direction - so yaw (horizontal alignment, which parallax also affects) is exactly as the board solve gave it; parallax is left to --shift-top/--shift-bottom.
scene_refinement.measured_on: take_20261003_133914 frames 0 and 3000 (vertical offset across the overlap: -11.8 px at the seam, -24 px per 1000 px across -> ~0 after)
scene_refinement.why: with a horizontal baseline, vertical offsets are distance-independent, so they pin the rotation without the tilt-vs-offset trade-off the close-range board solve suffers from. translation_mm is still the board solve (its ~4.6 mm vertical component is that same artifact); the stitcher uses only rotation_matrix.
